input: Set up a monthly one-on-one with my manager

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: It is unclear whether 'set up' means just sending a calendar invite, or also includes agreeing on an agenda structure, ground rules, or a shared doc — which changes how much prep work is involved.
Knowing the relationship dynamic (new manager, long-standing manager, remote vs. in-person) affects the tone and channel used to propose the meeting.
Whether a 1-on-1 already exists informally, was recently dropped, or has never existed changes what the first step is — revival vs. fresh proposal.
Preferred day, time-of-month anchor (first Monday, last Friday, etc.), and duration shape the actual invite details.
The tool or channel to use (calendar system, Slack, email, in-person ask) determines the immediate next action.
Whether the user wants to propose a structured agenda or keep it open-ended affects what supporting materials (if any) to prepare alongside the invite.
Knowing what 'done well' looks like — confirmed invite only, or also a first meeting successfully held — sets the finish line for this task.

gold.taskTitle: Set up a recurring monthly 1-on-1 with manager
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to establish a regular monthly one-on-one meeting with their manager, from initial outreach through to a confirmed recurring calendar invite.

questions.title: Has a regular 1-on-1 with your manager existed before?
questions.description: Determine whether this is a brand-new request, a revival of a lapsed meeting, or a formalisation of ad-hoc check-ins — this changes the opening approach entirely.

questions.title: What should 'set up' include beyond the calendar invite?
questions.description: Clarify whether the task ends at a confirmed recurring invite, or also includes drafting a shared agenda template, setting ground rules, or creating a running notes doc.

questions.title: How long have you worked with this manager?
questions.description: Understanding the relationship dynamic (new manager, established rapport, remote-only) shapes the tone and level of formality in how the meeting is proposed.

questions.title: What day, time, and duration do you have in mind?
questions.description: Pinning down the preferred slot (e.g., first Tuesday of the month, 30 min at 10 am) is essential for drafting the actual invite.

questions.title: How will you send the invite — calendar, email, or Slack?
questions.description: Identifying the tool or channel determines the immediate next action and any steps needed to get there.

questions.title: Should the meeting follow a set agenda or stay open-ended?
questions.description: Knowing whether the user wants a structured format (e.g., wins, blockers, career topics) versus a free-form chat affects what to prepare alongside the invite.

questions.title: What does success look like — invite confirmed or first meeting held?
questions.description: Establishing the finish line clarifies whether the task is complete once the manager accepts, or only after the first session has actually taken place.
